title: Human and anthropoid skulls show divergent rather than linear evolutionary change

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Human and anthropoid skulls show divergent rather than linear evolutionary change

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: No continuous transformation series passes through known fossil and living human and anthropoid skulls (Mesopithecus, Pithecanthropus, Neanderthal, modern man), indicating that there is no single straight line of descent and that their variation has been divergent.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The failure is not the fault of our method. It merely indicates that no one straight line of descent, or of consecutive transformation, exists; but on the contrary, that among human and anthropoid types, recent and extinct, we have to do with a complex problem of divergent, rather than of continuous, variation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Human and ape skulls”. Scope: fossil and living hominids and anthropoid apes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-17: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.92

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Divergence versus one serial lineage is a clear phylogenetic contrast. Extensive public genomic, fossil and morphological evidence covers the scope and standard methods strongly discriminate the alternatives.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare branching versus single-line models using genomic and morphological phylogenies of living and fossil hominids and apes. Robust non-ladder topology and incompatible transformation trajectories support divergent variation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil incompleteness affects exact branching order.

Historical taxon names require modern mapping.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The absence of a single straight series is a testable geometric claim, and many of the relevant crania have been measured or scanned. Open access and reconstruction choices are uneven for Pithecanthropus and Neanderthals especially. Existing material can reject some linear stories and cannot yet treat the full fossil sample as a clean public dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Ask whether one transformation series can be drawn through Mesopithecus, Homo erectus (Pithecanthropus), Neanderthals and modern humans with lower error than a branching arrangement of the same skulls. A large advantage for the branching model would support divergent change; a single series that passes through the fossils in order would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Which specimens are admitted as successive stages changes whether a straight series appears to fail.

Key fossils are few, often reconstructed, and unevenly available for download.
